data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"A decentralized network is more resilient to correlated failure than a centralized one because organic diversity in implementation stacks creates a 'stochastic firewall' against systemic software bugs.","counterconditions":[{"case":"The decentralized services all utilize a single, dominant shared dependency (e.g., a specific cloud provider's API or a single DNS root).","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"The failure is caused by a protocol-level flaw that affects all compliant implementations regardless of the stack.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"Decentralized services are developed by independent agents using diverse languages, libraries, and OS kernels (organic diversity). A single 'poison pill' input or a zero-day vulnerability in a specific library (e.g., Log4j) may crash a subset of the network, but the probability that all independent implementations share the same vulnerability is exponentially lower than the probability that a centralized service\u2014despite its internal redundancy\u2014shares a single monolithic codebase or unified configuration across all redundant nodes.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
